mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for three consecutive weeks (-84.9 to -66.3) alongside a parallel WORKPLACES recovery, indicating self-reinforcing mobility momentum that will continue into the next four weeks as routines normalize further.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -84.9 to -66.3 over three weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the prior 28-day mean despite continued WORKPLACES improvement.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden large jump in PARKS mobility (from -76.4 to -36.3 points, a 40-point week-on-week gain) signals a discrete relaxation of outdoor-activity restrictions that typically precedes a comparable rebound in RETAIL_REC within two weeks as broader public spaces reopen.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 30 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -76.4 to -36.3 between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks of a PARKS jump greater than 30 points, or declines instead.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility interacts to amplify retail footfall: commuters returning to offices via transit generate incidental retail and recreation visits that a single-series recovery would not fully capture, driving stronger RETAIL_REC gains over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved each of the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth rate is no greater when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise together than when only one rises, falsifying the interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: The steady decline in RESIDENTIAL time (30.6 to 20.6) reflects reduced stay-at-home behavior; under a reopening regime this behavioral shift frees time for discretionary retail and recreation trips, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 30.6 to 20.6 over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase even as RESIDENTIAL continues its downward trend, or RESIDENTIAL stabilizes while RETAIL_REC still rises, breaking the linkage.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility, a proxy for essential-only policy allowances, shows its week-on-week gain shrinking sharply (from +17.8 to +1.8 points), suggesting policy-driven reopening is plateauing; if this threshold holds, RETAIL_REC recovery will also stall within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM week-on-week gain falls below 5 points after two weeks of double-digit gains
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM gain decelerated from 17.8 to 1.8 points between consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues rising at the prior rate despite GROCERY_PHARM's deceleration, indicating no shared policy constraint.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp rise in PARKS mobility may reflect a seasonal shift toward outdoor recreation that substitutes for indoor retail and recreation visits, causing RETAIL_REC gains to slow or reverse over the next two weeks as people favor parks over shops.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility rises more than 10 points for two consecutive weeks while RETAIL_REC gain narrows
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose sharply while RETAIL_REC weekly gain shrank from 13.6 to 5.0 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise at a stable or accelerating rate even as PARKS mobility keeps climbing, disproving substitution.

mechanism_narrative: The deceleration in RETAIL_REC's own week-on-week improvement (13.6 points to 5.0 points) signals approaching behavioral saturation of pent-up demand, implying the next four weeks will show a smaller but still positive increase rather than continued rapid growth.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly gains decelerated from 13.6 to 5.0 points across the last two observed weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's 28-day mean fails to exceed the prior 28-day mean, indicating saturation has fully reversed momentum rather than merely slowing it.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent multi-week improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility indicates an active loosening-of-restrictions regime; under this regime, continued easing will further lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as more commercial and recreational venues reopen to full capacity.
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved in each of the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's 28-day mean does not exceed the prior period's mean despite sustained TRANSIT and WORKPLACES gains, indicating the regime assumption is invalid.
